author: reek
body: Stage one of two. This program stores a REAL PROGRAM in the fact store, revises it, checks the current tree back out, and prints it -- and what it prints is fed straight to the compiler by build/test-compile-from-store.ps1, which then runs the result.

author: reek
body: If that binary prints its greeting, a program was compiled out of the fact store. Storing Codex's own source has been the point since the founding document, and this is the first time it is literally true.

author: reek
body: On its own -- as a BVT test -- this pins the checkout BYTE FOR BYTE, because its expected output IS the source the store hands back. If a single character of the stored program is corrupted, reordered, truncated or superseded incorrectly, the expected file will not match, and it will not match in a way you can read.

author: reek
body: The first edition is WRONG ON PURPOSE. If the checkout ever takes it, the compiled binary announces the fact instead of the greeting, and stage two fails loudly rather than passing a lie.
